# MCP server boundary

CRITICAL VISUAL RULE: communicate only through boundaries, paths, gates, and abstract objects. Keep every surface blank. Do not draw the GitHub logo, Mona, Octocat, Invertocat, the Copilot mascot, wordmarks, letters, numbers, code, charts, interface controls, badges, or labeled icons.

Create premium animated 16:9 GitHub key art, composed safely inside a 3:2 generation canvas. Render a bright conceptual 2.5D scene on a white and cool off-white background with subtle contribution-grid texture, luminous network paths, crisp Octicon-inspired geometry, soft neutral shadows, and restrained depth. Use approximately 80% white or off-white, 10% neutral gray, 5% GitHub green, and 5% Copilot purple.

Show four distinct abstract objects representing tools, resources, prompts, and context approaching an explicit server boundary. Authentication, authorization, and data-scope gates must visibly allow some paths and stop others. The visual metaphor must immediately communicate controlled exposure across a clear permission boundary while remaining conceptual and vendor-neutral.

Keep the upper-left 40% calm for the exact native slide title. Leave a clean foreground position outside the boundary where approved, unmodified mascot artwork can be layered later in Slidev. No people, mascots, logos, generic robots, words, letters, fake UI, screenshots, invented MCP logo, dark panels, trademark adaptations, or watermarks.
